verdict.rationale: Docs explicitly state plugins expose 'server-backed capabilities' via MCP (docs-33) and that a plugin 'can contain skills, MCP servers, or both' including 'a remote MCP-only plugin' (docs-40), with plugin-creator adding 'MCP server wiring' (docs-15). The official openai/plugins marketplace lists named first-party MCP-backed plugins (Notion, Slack, Figma) installable via `/plugins` or `codex plugin marketplace add`, giving Codex agents a documented path to connect via official MCP servers. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on confirmation that connecting to a specific official MCP server plugin works end-to-end, and detail on authentication/config for the MCP connection itself.
